notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no WAF/robots block. Found /new-in in the main mega-menu (link text 'New In') and confirmed via Magento GraphQL categoryList: id 491, name 'New In', url_path 'new-in', product_count 270, with 5 real children (Accessories, Bedroom, Dining Room, Living Room, Garden) each a distinct url_path -- genuine site-defined sub-structure, preserved as grouping row + leaves. All 6 pages render via the same <category-view> component as ordinary category pages (real product grids, filters, sort options), not editorial pages; parent H1 = 'New In'. Products load client-side via Searchspring (siteId zzw53h); used Playwright to capture the live search.json totalResults and the rendered 'N Products' text. Applied the site-wide Searchspring +1-phantom-result offset (totalResults minus 1) established this session (see cl85.json/bs85.json notes) -- for New In and New In>Accessories this was independently double-confirmed against BOTH a live-rendered 'N Products' string AND the Magento product_count value, which matched exactly (New In>Accessories: Magento 17, Searchspring 18-1=17, rendered '17 Products'; New In>Bedroom Magento 41 vs SS 42-1=41; New In>Dining Room Magento 39 vs SS 40-1=39; New In>Living Room Magento 161 vs SS 162-1=161; New In>Garden Magento 1 vs SS 2-1=1). Parent total (272) does not equal the sum of the 5 children (259) -- expected overlap/non-exhaustive-tagging behaviour, not an error (some New In products may not carry a subcategory tag, or overlap across subcategories). Checked the site's own taxonomy for other new-arrivals-type pages/terms (New Collection, What's New, Just In, Latest) via sitemap.xml keyword grep and mega-menu/footer inspection -- none found beyond the /new-in tree; no separate microsite equivalent to the Clearance outlet site exists for New Arrivals. No local-language variant needed (UK/English site).
